items.title: No steering wheel, no problem: Can Tesla speed by Cybercab probe?
items.summary: Federal investigators have opened an investigation into whether Tesla's (TSLA) new Cybercabs comply with federal safety standards, just as the company begins testing its service in Austin, Texas.  Market Domination host Josh Lipton is joined by Tom Narayan, RBC Capital Markets lead equity analyst for global autos, to discuss if the investigation jeopardizes the rollout and how Tesla is also trying to avoid an "Apple Maps moment."

items.title: Tech stocks today: Tesla's Cybercab event fails to impress, Feds launch investigation into the robotaxi

items.title: Tesla (TSLA) Faces NHTSA Cybercab Safety Probe After Austin Robotaxi Rollout
items.summary: US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opens investigation into Tesla (NasdaqGS:TSLA) Cybercab robotaxi safety compliance after commercial rollout in Austin, Texas. Probe centers on whether Cybercab vehicles without traditional steering wheels and pedals meet federal motor vehicle safety standards. Review focuses on Tesla's self-certification process and how the company addresses occupant safety in fully autonomous commercial service. Investigation outcome may affect regulatory...

items.title: Tesla (TSLA) Stock Trades Down, Here Is Why
items.summary: Shares of electric vehicle pioneer Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) fell 6% in the afternoon session after U.S. safety regulators said they were evaluating the rollout of the company's new Cybercab, compounding a sell-the-news reaction to a launch event.

items.title: Self-Driving’s Next Task: Potholes
items.summary: REVIEW  On Monday, shares of Tesla jumped 5.5%, closing at $367.95, up 18% for the month after dropping 26% in July. Why the rise? There were no Wall Street upgrades or price-target changes. One Global exchange-traded fund co-founder Gary Black speculated investors might be anticipating the launch of Cybercab, Tesla’s robo-taxi, which lacks a steering wheel.
